doc.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Closing thanks and the next set
summary: Closing remarks, a reminder to practice rhythm, and thanks; he has a last 10:30 set to play.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Oh, thank you. I’ve enjoyed it. It’s very nice to be part of your project.
All you drummers out there, remember that thing about practicing rhythm.

Yeah, that’s right. If you’re going to be a good rhythm player, it’s a really a good idea to practice some rhythm, yeah, and get good. And you know what I tell my students? I’m going to teach you to be a rhythm expert who plays the drums. And hopefully a good musician, you know, I mean those two things. But that’s really what it’s about. And if you’re out there propagating, especially about jazz, I think you should talk about the important things, I really do.
Alright. Well on behalf of the Hamilton Jazz Archive, we’d like to thank Ed Shaughnessy for his time with us today.
He’s on his way to play another set.
Yeah, I’ve got time to have supper and play the last 10:30 set. That’s my last one.
Thank you. That’s for inviting me. I appreciate it. Thank you. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-
